related_questions.question: Are they still recommending COVID shots?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, COVID-19 vaccines, including updated versions for the 2024-2025 season, are still recommended, especially for those at higher risk of severe illness. While they may not completely prevent infection, they significantly reduce the risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death.
Here's why updated COVID-19 vaccines are still recommended:

list.title: Reduced Severity:
list.snippet: Updated vaccines offer strong protection against severe disease, including hospitalization and death, particularly for those at higher risk.

list.title: Protection for Vulnerable Groups:
list.snippet: The CDC recommends that certain individuals, including those 65 and older, those with underlying health conditions, and pregnant individuals, get the latest COVID-19 vaccine.

list.title: Protection from New Variants:
list.snippet: Updated vaccines are designed to target the currently circulating strains of the virus, providing better protection than older versions.

list.title: Decreasing Immunity:
list.snippet: Immunity from infection and vaccination can decrease over time, making updated vaccines necessary for maintaining adequate protection.

text_blocks.snippet: Ultimately, if you are eligible for the COVID-19 vaccine, it's recommended to stay up-to-date to protect yourself and those around you, especially those at higher risk.

related_questions.question: When will the new COVID vaccine be available in 2025?

text_blocks.snippet: The updated COVID-19 vaccines for the 2025-2026 season in the United States are expected to be available in the fall of 2025, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov). The FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee (VRBPAC) has recommended a monovalent JN.1-lineage vaccine for this season. The CDC also recommends a 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine for most adults 18 and older.
